summary: CI build cache decryption fails after S3 SSE-KMS rewrap; release pipelines stuck in Prepare stage
description:
Issue summary:
After an automated KMS key rewrap for the S3 bucket used as the CI build cache (s3://redwood-ci-cache), CI jobs started failing to fetch cached layers. Runners report cache decryption errors and several release pipelines have been stuck in the 'Prepare' phase for ~3 hours.

Impact:
- Multiple release pipelines (canary + stable) are blocked and cannot proceed past dependency fetch.
- Queue length for release runners on prod-us-east increased from ~10 to ~65 pending jobs.
- Increased build times for affected jobs (cold builds) and risk of missing release windows.

Environment:
- Environment: prod-us-east
- Components affected: CI runner pool, artifact cache (S3), KMS key used for SSE-KMS, release pipelines

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger a release pipeline that uses the cached build layers from s3://redwood-ci-cache.
2) Runner attempts GET object with SSE-KMS; S3 returns 403 and logs a KMS:Decrypt failure in CloudTrail for the envelope key.
3) Job enters retry loop and eventually reports cache fetch failure and keeps the pipeline stuck in Prepare.

Relevant logs and signals:
- CloudTrail shows Decrypt failures for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-efgh-1234 at 2026-03-10T02:14:03Z.
- S3 access logs show x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id changed at 2026-03-10T01:58:12Z (rewrap event).
- Runner logs (build-rt-03) excerpt: "ERROR: cache decryption failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key ..."
- CI queue metric: runner_pending_count.prod-us-east increased to 65 at peak.

Hypothesis / initial investigation:
- An automated KMS rewrap job rotated the envelope keys for the bucket. New key policy/aliases introduced a tighter principal restriction that excludes the CI runner role used by self-hosted runners. As a result, S3 objects now require the new key for decryption but the runner IAM principal lacks kms:Decrypt on the new key.
- Alternative hypothesis: the key ID alias moved to a different account (cross-account rewrap) and the runner role's trust policy is missing a condition.

Temporary mitigation observed to work:
- Restoring previous key alias (alias/ci-cache-prev) allowed runners to decrypt objects again for a subset of objects that retained the old key metadata.
- Manually granting kms:Decrypt on the new key to the runner role allowed a single test pipeline to proceed (verified by SRE:ened).

Workaround applied so far:
- SRE temporarily added kms:Decrypt permission for role arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-runner-prod to the new key policy to restore immediate pipeline throughput. This is a mitigation only; revert requires discussion with security.

Investigation notes:
- Security change log shows an automated rewrap executed by the key-rotation Lambda at 2026-03-10T01:55Z. The Lambda replaced the CMK alias and updated key policy according to the new template which restricts decrypt to a narrower set of principals.
- There is a gap: key-rotation Lambda repo (github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation) PR #78 changed the policy template; linked PR reference: github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation/pull/78.
- A runbook for KMS rewrap exists but does not include a validation step to confirm CI IAM principals are listed in new policy.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Security & SRE to coordinate a controlled update to the key policy: re-add ci-runner-prod role as delegated decrypt principal and add automated verification test that simulates runner decrypt request.
2) Update key-rotation Lambda to include a post-rotation validation step that runs a decrypt check using a staging object and the CI principal.
3) Backfill: scan S3 objects to identify those re-encrypted under the new key and verify access patterns. Confirm if any objects lost previous key metadata.
4) Add a pre-rotation change-control gating in Confluence and Slack (#infra-ops) to notify Release Engineering 24 hours before rewraps that impact shared caches.

Related links:
- CloudTrail event sample: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=us-east-1
- Key rotation repo PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation/pull/78
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/KMS+Key+Rotation+Runbook

Resolution status:
- Mitigation in place (temporary key policy change). Full remediation pending policy update and CI validation automation.

investigation_notes: Key-rotation Lambda changed key alias and policy without running a decrypt validation using the CI principal. CloudTrail confirms Decrypt failures started immediately after alias swap. There is an existing review step in the rotation PR but no automated verification. SRE verified temporary policy grant restores functionality; security wants formal change and audit log. Will add a preflight decrypt test to the Lambda and a Confluence change notice. Expected ETA for full remediation: 2026-03-16.
workaround: Temporarily granted kms:Decrypt on new CMK to role arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-runner-prod. This restored pipeline throughput. Workaround is temporary and should be revoked after policy fix and validation are in place.
next_steps: 1) Security to approve adding ci-runner role to key policy with audit comments. 2) Infra to patch key-rotation Lambda to run decrypt verification and rollback on failure. 3) Release Eng to be notified 24h prior to next rewrap. 4) Post-incident: add test to release pipeline that validates cache decrypt during PRs that touch infra-key-rotation.
resolution: Mitigation applied; awaiting permanent policy update and automation.
